### Scansion: hand scan of 338

`ὦ υἱὲ Πετεῶο διοτρεφέος βασιλῆος` has 16 syllables if no vowel is merged: ὦ · υἱ · ὲ · Πε · τε · ῶ · ο · δι · ο · τρε · φέ · ος · βα · σι · λῆ · ος. The second half is regular: δι-ο | τρε-φέ-ος | βα-σι-λῆ-ος fills the end of foot 3 and feet 4 to 6 as a feminine caesura and two dactyls with the closing spondee (`λῆος` as one long syllable by synizesis). The first half cannot be made regular. Feet 1 and 2 need ὦ υἱ (two longs, υι a diphthong) and then a long syllable at the start of foot 2, but the next syllable is the final ε of υἱέ, short, followed by Πε-, a single consonant that makes no position. Resolving ὦ υ-ι as a dactyl does not help: the same short ε then opens foot 2. Hiatus before υἱέ is no help either (ὦ is long in any case at the start of the line). The scanner's own answer is the same (`metrical lengthening: υἱὲ [longum of foot 2]`, UNRESOLVED). The irregularity is real as transmitted, so the sentence was added to the note. No other line of the part is flagged.

### The 362 missing-stop question (README rule 5)

Checked and not acted on. The pinned source reads `ἀλλ’ ἴθι ταῦτα δ’ ὄπισθεν ἀρεσσόμεθ’ εἴ τι κακὸν νῦν / εἴρηται, τὰ δὲ πάντα θεοὶ μεταμώνια θεῖεν.` with no mark after ἴθι and ἀρεσσόμεθ’ and a comma after εἴρηται. Rule 5 lets a run add a mark only where the printed edition (Monro and Allen, 1920) has it, or where an already-published part prints it for the same line; neither 4.362 nor 4.363 stands in a published part, and the Monro–Allen page is not available in this environment (archive.org is blocked; the Perseus TEI is the pinned source itself, sha256 identical, so it cannot be a second witness; the other copies found on GitHub derive from it or are the papyrus edition DCLP, which prints `ἴθι,·` by its own punctuation, not the OCT's). I will not re-pin on memory of a different edition (Murray's Loeb, whose English suggests a stop after the clause, is not Allen). The source is therefore unchanged and `parts.json` is not touched. The unit split at `εἴρηται,` stands: comma-final units are normal in this poem (iliad-012, -013, -014, -022 have 14–19 each) because the source drops many commas and the sense-units in practice end where the clause closes; the note says the comma ends the unit. If a person with the OCT finds `εἴρηται·` or `ἴθι·` printed, the fix is one mark in the source file, a new `sha256` for iliad-024 only (362 is in no other part), and the unit boundary at 362 would then already be right.
